Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
First-person pronouns do not show a distinct ergative form; the same pronoun form is used for transitive A and intransitive S.
Second-person pronouns do not show a distinct ergative form; the same pronoun form is used for transitive A and intransitive S.
Third-person pronouns show ergative alignment; distinct agent forms exist.
Full NPs exhibit ergative alignment with agent markers 'an' (common NPs) and 'ru' (oblique/focused NPs).
Ergative alignment occurs in the imperfective aspect.
Ergative alignment occurs in the perfective aspect.
Ergative alignment occurs in past tense clauses.
Ergative alignment is applied in non-past tenses.
Ergative alignment occurs in sentences in the indicative mood.
Ergative alignment occurs in non-indicative moods.
Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with realis status.
Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with irrealis status.
Ergative alignment exists in the context of an agentive A argument.
Ergative alignment exists in the context of a non-agentive A argument.

When A is thematized (fronted to pre-verbal position), the ergative marker is OBLIGATORILY removed (Bril 2002: §3.7.1, p.57: 'Le sujet thématisé du verbe transitif apparaît sans les marques d'agent an ou ru').
When A is not thematized (basic VSO order), the ergative marker is present.
Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with an animate A.
Ergative alignment occurs in clauses with an inanimate A.
Ergative alignment occurs in main clauses.
Non-main clauses exhibit ergative alignment.
Ergative alignment is conditioned by thematization: when A is fronted to initial position (SVO structure), the ergative marker is obligatorily removed. This is the additional conditioning factor.

The agent marker 'an' is historically derived from the possessive/genitive marker; emphatic agent constructions productively combine the agent base with genitive suffixes (Bril 2002: 52). ERG=GEN confirmed.
The agent marker 'ru' (used for focused/oblique agent NPs) also functions as the instrumental marker (Bril 2002: 153). Comitative uses different markers (bole-/ma). ERG=INST confirmed.
